QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_20

question.text: If a Cat III AIF's NAV has only decreased since inception, the High-Water Mark is taken as:

answer.text: Initial subscription price of units issued by the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook specifies a direct fallback rule for HWM: if the NAV of the Cat III AIF has only decreased since inception, the High-Water Mark is taken as the initial subscription price of the units issued by the fund. The Trap: Zero, the prior year-end NAV, and the called-capital amount are not the workbook's specified HWM fallback when NAV has only decreased since inception. Note: The fallback HWM rule is taken from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
